turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not afraid of the Mussulmans, but I will not tolerate injustice against my people. Your actions are causing unrest and division.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your people, Nikhil? Or your tenants? Your tenants are human beings, not subjects of a petty king. You speak of division, but who is the divider? You who demand loyalty and obedience, or I who seek freedom and justice?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric may sound noble, Sandip, but it is a guise for your exploitation. My tenants are my responsibility, and I will not let you undermine my authority or their well-being.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Exploitation, you say? I call it liberation, Nikhil. Your tenants are not pawns in your little game of power, they are the future of our nation. And I will not stand idly by while you squander their potential with your outdated notions of control and possession.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your so-called liberation is nothing but a facade for your own ambition, Sandip. You speak of freedom but offer only chaos. My tenants need stability and protection, not the kind of revolution that leaves them worse off.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Chaos, Nikhil? I call it the spark of change. Stability is the comfort of the status quo, but change is the breath of life. Your tenants are not just faces in a crowd, they are the heart of our nation's pulse.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your spark of change is a flame of discord, Sandip. My people need a leader who provides light, not one who only ignites fear and division.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fear and division? Nikhil, you speak as if the people are sheep, content with their meekness. But I see them as lions, ready to roar and claim their rightful place in the sun.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sheep or lions, Sandip, your methods make them prey. I come to warn you, not just for my own sake, but for theirs. Cease your oppressive actions or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your heart is in the right place, Nikhil, but your eyes are blind to the fire in their souls. Consequences? I welcome them as a test of our resolve. The people will be my shield and my sword.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your resolve is reckless, Sandip. The people need guidance, not just a voice that echoes their anger. Your actions endanger us all.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Reckless? Perhaps. But it takes a spark to light a fire, Nikhil. The people are not just spectators in this drama, they are the stars. And I am merely the stage on which they perform their destiny.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may sound noble, Sandip, but your actions are a powder keg waiting to ignite. I urge you to reconsider your path before it's too late.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Noble? Perhaps. But noble deeds are often the ones that shake the foundations of the old world. And in this tempest, it is the storm that shapes the future, not the calm.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric is stirring, but it is the reality of threats and instability that will determine our fate. I cannot stand idly by while you jeopardize the safety and livelihood of my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh Nikhil, your heart is pure, but your vision is narrow. The safety you speak of is a cage, not a sanctuary. The storm I bring is the breath of life, not the whisper of death.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I... I feel caught between your words, Sandip, and Nikhil's concerns. Can there be a middle ground where both safety and change can coexist?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, I understand your dilemma, but the safety of our people should come before any abstract notion of change. Sandip's actions are reckless and dangerous.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I wish to believe there is a way to balance your visions, but I see the fear in your tenants' eyes, Sandip. Can we not find a path that does not lead to such dread?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, my beloved, do not be swayed by Nikhil's myopic fears. The path I tread is the path of the future, where the old chains of servitude give way to the bright sun of independence.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
